text:
sara (support): Hey — customer (acct: acme-corp, user: aj@acme.com) is hitting a 401 right after the SSO redirect. They say it briefly showed a billing page then 401. Happened ~2025-08-14 15:12 UTC. They don't have a HAR yet, can we send a minimal capture checklist?

maria (eng): Yes — please ask them to capture: console + network HAR and one cURL of the failing request. Key bits we need: exact timestamp, user email, and any X-Request-Id or x-rw-request-id header. If they can't find the header, HAR is still fine.

jordan (devex): Minimal Chrome steps I usually paste:
1) Open Chrome DevTools (F12) -> Network tab.
2) Check: "Preserve log" and "Disable cache".
3) Reproduce the flow (SSO redirect -> hit 401).
4) Right-click in Network list -> "Save all as HAR with content".
5) Open Console panel -> right-click -> "Save as..." (or copy visible messages).
6) If they can, click the failing network row -> Headers -> look for `x-request-id` (or `x-rw-request-id`) and paste it into the ticket.

Include this short curl reproduction instruction too: right-click failing request -> Copy -> Copy as cURL (bash). Ask them to paste that cURL into the thread (they should redact Authorization). Example we give them to run after redaction:```
# run locally to see full response headers/body
curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/endpoint' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'X-Request-Id: 123e4567-89ab' -v
```

maria (eng): If they use Safari on mac / iOS:
- macOS Safari: Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network -> Preserve Log -> reproduce -> Export -> File -> Save as HAR.
- iOS Safari: connect device to mac, enable "Develop" menu in Safari, open the page on device, use Develop->iPhone -> Inspect -> Save Network.

jordan (devex): Android / Chrome on device: enable USB debugging -> chrome://inspect on desktop -> inspect device -> Network -> reproduce -> Save HAR.

support-bot: Tip: if customer is uncomfortable sharing tokens, they should redact Authorization headers and session cookies. Provide exact times and the user email — that helps us find matching logs on our side.

sara (support): Also ask them to attach a short step-by-step (which button they clicked, whether they were on incognito or company-managed device) and a screenshot of the final 401 page.

maria (eng): Small handy commands for them to strip secrets from the HAR before upload (optional):
```bash
# redact Authorization header from har.json
sed -E 's/(Authorization\":\s\")[^\"]+\"/\1REDACTED\"/g' har.json > har.redacted.json
# or gzip to upload
gzip -c har.redacted.json > har.redacted.json.gz
```

jordan (devex): One more: ask them to also save the cURL as text and run it with `-i -v` so we can see response headers (we look for our request id and upstream status).

sara (support): If they can't produce HAR, an exported Network -> "Copy -> Copy as cURL" for the failing request + console log is the minimum.

maria (eng): If they include an X-Request-Id, paste it here or in the support portal when uploading. Our log retention lets us correlate within ~2 weeks but having the exact timestamp speeds things up.

sara (support): I'll send this checklist to the customer now. If they upload, I'll attach the file here and ping you both. Thanks :thumbsup:

maria (eng): thanks — if you see any 502 / gateway traces in the HAR, flag it and we can escalate to eng-infra.

support-bot: Automated reminder: when a HAR is attached, please also include the first_message_ts and approximate user local time to help correlate logs.
